Subject: Quick: trial credits request (FastFlow pilot)

Hi Priyom,

Hope you're well — we just onboarded a pilot project with two internal teams and noticed that a handful of new signups were eligible for the promotional trial credits. Can you confirm the auto-issuance window and whether we can apply an extension for one of the accounts while they finish a demo next week?

The account names are: FastFlow - data-team (lead: Raj Mehta) and FastFlow - infra (lead: L. Chen).

Attached are CSV exports of the signup records from our side. One thing to flag: the infra signup shows several similar device fingerprints across four emails; ops asked us to double-check if those should be allowed. Appreciate any guidance — we don't want to block a legitimate pilot but also want to avoid abuse.

Thanks,
Ayesha
Senior Partnerships Manager
FastFlow.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick: trial credits request (FastFlow pilot)

Marissa / Neha — forwarding for fraud ops triage. Ayesha from FastFlow flagged repeated device fingerprints across multiple signups; they want an extension for one account if it's legitimate. Can you review the CSV and the device_report (ops included) and advise whether to:

- approve extension and issue additional 1,000 free credits,
- approve but mark for rate limits / 30-day probation, or
- deny and ask FastFlow to re-onboard via SSO/SCIM?

Dev, tagging you to pull any kernel-level rate/batch logs if you need to correlate IPs or GPU usage patterns.

Quick context: FastFlow is a mid-stage PLG prospect; we prioritize not blocking pilot customers, but we've seen organized signup clusters from rotating disposable domains tied to device replay before.

Priyom
Growth — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the flag — looked through the CSV. Summary notes: 

- There are 6 signups in two hours from the same /24 with different emails at disposable providers.
- Device fingerprint hashes are very similar but not identical; likely a headless browser with small entropy changes (common in bot toolkits).
- No prior activity from those accounts beyond token generation attempts; two accounts used the free credits and attempted >500k tokens within the first hour (very suspicious).

My recommendation: do not auto-approve an extension. Offer a one-time manual review path: require SSO (or a confirmation call) for the infra team contact (L. Chen) before issuing any additional credits. For the data-team pilot (Raj Mehta), their email domain matches corporate records and shows prior engagement — we can approve a 7-day extension with a 30k token cap and put them on probation monitoring.

I'll attach a short device_fingerprint_report.pdf with the anomaly graph. If Growth wants to keep the relationship warm, offer FastFlow a demo extension contingent on completing SSO.

-Marissa
Senior Fraud Ops Analyst

Attachments: device_fingerprint_report.pdf (PDF stub)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha@fastflow.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credits flagged — repeated device signals on FastFlow trial signups

Hi Ayesha — thanks for the patience. We investigated and landed on a conservative, customer-friendly path: 

1) For FastFlow - infra (L. Chen): hold issuance pending SSO confirmation or a short verification call. We've placed those accounts on hold and revoked the unused portion of trial credits. If you can share the SSO admin contact or schedule a 15-min verification call, we will process the extension immediately after verification.

2) For FastFlow - data-team (Raj Mehta): approved a one-time trial extension (1,000 free credits) with a monitoring cap of 30k tokens during the next 7 days. We'll watch for spikes; Marissa's team will auto-flag any >60% deviation from expected usage patterns.

3) We've opened a short incident ticket (HS-FF-2025-09-30) in HubSpot and attached the reports to the record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/contact/FF-7890. We also included the device report and signup CSV in the drive folder.

If FastFlow prefers, we can also whiteboard a custom pilot gating flow (SSO + IP allowlist) to avoid future friction.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
